messages.subject: MSstats.daily 2.1.6 feedback
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I've tried MSstats.daily 2.1.6 on some test data (label-free DDA) and am happy to say that it works for me now. Thanks for fixing the problems that I reported before!

If I may express some - hopefully constructive - criticism, here are some aspects that I think could still be improved:
1. I've noticed that log files ("msstats.log") are now produced in the working directory - where I don't want them. How can I change this?
2. In the "transformMSnSetToMSstats" function: "data" should be the first (not the last) parameter, because it is the primary input and doesn't have a default value.
3. In "groupComparisonPlots(..., "VolcanoPlot", FCcutoff=x): An option to print protein names only for proteins that pass the FDR and fold-change cut-offs (those shown in blue/red) would be useful.
4. "groupComparisonPlots"/"dataProcessPlots": You should split these into individual functions for the different plots (if there is common code between them, move it into helper functions). Currently these functions contain parameters that are mutually exclusive and only work for some of the plots, which makes things confusing. On the implementation side, you currently have one function that is unnecessarily long and complex (and thus hard to maintain/improve).

Cheers

Hendrik

Dea Mark,

If you assign the name of subdirectory,xyz, you can use address="xyz/" (add slash to distinguish that this is the folder name). Then 'ProfilePlot.pdf' file will be generated in 'xyz' folder under the working directory.

messages.subject: iTRAQ and SILAC analyses
messages.body_plain:
Dear developers,
first of all, thanks for your efforts in making MSstats available to the community. I've been using it with my shotgun label-free data for some time and am pretty happy with the results.

A while ago I heard (or read) somewhere that you guys were working on a new version to deal with iTRAQ/TMT data. I just wanted to follow up on this one. Can we expect a MSstats version to deal with iTRAQ/TMT experiments? If so, should it be soon or may take some time?
One more thing, can we use MSstats for SILAC experiments as it was a SRM experiment with a reference peptide? In practice I think that it is feasible, however I am not sure whether it is statistically sounding. In other words, I guess that MSstats uses certain statistical assumptions for SRM experiments with SIL peptides that apply to such SRM experiments only and maybe are not applicable to SILAC studies. What is your point of view on this??
Again, thank you for MSstats!
Best regards
Alex

messages.subject: Re: iTRAQ and SILAC analyses
messages.body_plain:
Dear Alex,

Thank you very much for the positive feedback!

For SILAC experiments, where a reference sample is added to every endogenous sample in a constant concentration, MSstats can be used as is. We recommend to look at the profile plots to have a sense of the nature of interferences, and remove run x feature (and possibly condition x feature) interactions if the interferences appear random.

For SILAC experiments where two endogenous samples (e.g. one from each group) are mixed together, MSstats should be applicable in principle. However we haven't had a chance to benchmark it thoroughly, we plan to do this shortly.

For TMT and iTRAQ things are more complicated, since the quantification occurs at the MS2 level, and MS2 spectra create an additional blocking structure. We currently do not account for this in the model. We plan to investigate this in the future, however it will likely to take some time.

I hope that this clarifies things for you somewhat. Thank you again for using MSstats.

Sincerely
Olga

messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
messages.body_plain:
Dear Lorenzo,

I am glad that you could make progress. Regarding shared ions: currently we do require that a (modified) peptide sequence is uniquely mapped to a protein. If an ion belongs to multiple proteins than its abundance has contributions from multiple sources, and it will negatively affect individual protein-level quantifications. In theory it is possible to view the abundance of shared ions as a mixture and deconvolute it computationally, but we don't implement this yet. In practice we suggest to either exclude these ions from protein-level analysis, or work with peptide-level quantification as opposed to protein-level quantification. If you are interested in PTMs, peptide-level quantification may be more appropriate. (In this case, just use peptide names in the protein name column).

I hope that this helps at least somewhat
Sincerely
Olga

I noticed that peptides with variable modifications where, for instance, both methionine oxidized and native forms of the same peptide are identified, are considered as duplicates by MSstats...
I had to delete one of them to process data.

Kind Regards

Filippo

messages.subject: Re: MSstats 2.1.3 released!!
messages.body_plain:
Dear Filippo,

An alternative is to change the naming convention, and alter the name of the peptide that contains a PTM. A peptide ion will be considered unique if it is represented by a unique string of characters.

Best wishes
Olga

messages.subject_clean: MSstats in Skyline with different version of R
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to have the MSstats with Skyline run with different (higher) version of R? I have R3.1 installed on my computer and do not want to clutter it with addition of another version of R. Is there a way to get Skyline and MSstats work with R3.1 if I get the required packages installed?

Thanks,

Tomas
